issues.description: The Bitmap24 class header in the template declares the constructors, destructor and all member functions as private, but the solution's header exposes them as public. User code in main.cpp instantiates Bitmap24 and calls its public methods (resize_buffer, set, save). Having the constructors and methods private in the template prevents students from using the class as intended and will cause compilation errors or confusion when following the example/solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructors, destructor and the public interface (resize_buffer, save, set) public in the template's Bitmap24.hpp, matching the solution. Specifically, change the 'private:' section so that data members remain private but add a 'public:' section exposing the constructors, destructor, and public methods used by main.cpp. This preserves encapsulation while allowing students to compile and run the example code.
